Topics · Meaning and purpose

Must I stand for justice even against my family?

True witness even against self and parents, with kindness. A justice that keeps love and puts no one at risk.

Part 1 of 3

﴿يَـٰٓأَيُّهَا ٱلَّذِينَ ءَامَنُوا۟ كُونُوا۟ قَوَّٰمِينَ بِٱلْقِسْطِ شُهَدَآءَ لِلَّهِ وَلَوْ عَلَىٰٓ أَنفُسِكُمْ أَوِ ٱلْوَٰلِدَيْنِ وَٱلْأَقْرَبِينَ ۚ إِن يَكُنْ غَنِيًّا أَوْ فَقِيرًا فَٱللَّهُ أَوْلَىٰ بِهِمَا ۖ فَلَا تَتَّبِعُوا۟ ٱلْهَوَىٰٓ أَن تَعْدِلُوا۟ ۚ وَإِن تَلْوُۥٓا۟ أَوْ تُعْرِضُوا۟ فَإِنَّ ٱللَّهَ كَانَ بِمَا تَعْمَلُونَ خَبِيرًا﴾

Translation of the meaning

O you who have believed, be persistently standing firm in justice, witnesses for Allāh, even if it be against yourselves or parents and relatives. Whether one is rich or poor, Allāh is more worthy of both.[223] So follow not [personal] inclination, lest you not be just. And if you distort [your testimony] or refuse [to give it], then indeed Allāh is ever, of what you do, Aware.

Translator's notes

[223] i.e., more knowledgeable of their best interests. Therefore, adhere to what He has enjoined upon you and testify honestly.

Quran · An-Nisa 4:135

Translation

“‘You shall do no injustice in judgment. You shall not be partial to the poor, nor show favoritism to the great; but you shall judge your neighbor in righteousness.

Original · Hebrew

לֹא־תַעֲשׂ֥וּ עָ֨וֶל֙ בַּמִּשְׁפָּ֔ט לֹא־תִשָּׂ֣א פְנֵי־דָ֔ל וְלֹ֥א תֶהְדַּ֖ר פְּנֵ֣י גָד֑וֹל בְּצֶ֖דֶק תִּשְׁפֹּ֥ט עֲמִיתֶֽךָ׃

the Torah (Leviticus) · 19:15

World English Bible

If justice stopped at the edge of your family, it would be loyalty and not justice. One who applies a rule to others and exempts their own has no rule. The verse starts with the hardest case: stand firm for fairness, witnesses for God, even against yourselves. Then parents and near kin. Notice the order: the self comes first. Justice starts with honesty about you, before it reaches anyone else.

A question for you

What is hardest for you?

If you sayTo be truthful about myself.
ThenThe verse starts there, so you are at its beginning.
If you sayTo stand against my family.
ThenA real question, and the last part reads a verse on kindness to them alongside it.
If you sayIt might not be safe for me.
ThenYour safety matters. 2:286 says no soul is charged beyond its capacity. Talk with someone you trust or a service that can help; this Step does not decide for you.

Part 2 of 3

﴿يَـٰٓأَيُّهَا ٱلَّذِينَ ءَامَنُوا۟ كُونُوا۟ قَوَّٰمِينَ لِلَّهِ شُهَدَآءَ بِٱلْقِسْطِ ۖ وَلَا يَجْرِمَنَّكُمْ شَنَـَٔانُ قَوْمٍ عَلَىٰٓ أَلَّا تَعْدِلُوا۟ ۚ ٱعْدِلُوا۟ هُوَ أَقْرَبُ لِلتَّقْوَىٰ ۖ وَٱتَّقُوا۟ ٱللَّهَ ۚ إِنَّ ٱللَّهَ خَبِيرٌۢ بِمَا تَعْمَلُونَ﴾

Translation of the meaning

O you who have believed, be persistently standing firm for Allāh, witnesses in justice, and do not let the hatred of a people prevent you from being just. Be just; that is nearer to righteousness. And fear Allāh; indeed, Allāh is [fully] Aware of what you do.

Quran · Al-Ma'idah 5:8

Translation

You shall not pervert justice. You shall not show partiality. You shall not take a bribe, for a bribe blinds the eyes of the wise and perverts the words of the righteous. You shall follow that which is altogether just, that you may live and inherit the land which Yahweh your God gives you.

Original · Hebrew

לֹא־תַטֶּ֣ה מִשְׁפָּ֔ט לֹ֥א תַכִּ֖יר פָּנִ֑ים וְלֹא־תִקַּ֣ח שֹׁ֔חַד כִּ֣י הַשֹּׁ֗חַד יְעַוֵּר֙ עֵינֵ֣י חֲכָמִ֔ים וִֽיסַלֵּ֖ף דִּבְרֵ֥י צַדִּיקִֽם׃ צֶ֥דֶק צֶ֖דֶק תִּרְדֹּ֑ף לְמַ֤עַן תִּֽחְיֶה֙ וְיָרַשְׁתָּ֣ אֶת־הָאָ֔רֶץ אֲשֶׁר־יְהוָ֥ה אֱלֹהֶ֖יךָ נֹתֵ֥ן לָֽךְ׃

the Torah (Deuteronomy) · 16:19-20

World English Bible

The second test is the reverse: hating a people. As love pulls toward favouritism, resentment pulls toward injustice. The verse says: do not let hatred of a people lead you away from fairness. Be fair. Justice follows feeling in neither direction. It is measured by what happened, and not by who the other side is. And the verse says this is nearer to piety.

A question for you

Compare the two tests. Which is harder for you?

If you sayBeing fair with those I love.
ThenThen the first verse is nearest to you.
If you sayBeing fair with those I dislike.
ThenThe verse speaks of a whole people. A Step on fairness toward people of other faiths is open to you.
If you saySometimes I do not know what justice is.
ThenA rare honesty. Justice begins right there: in hearing both sides.

Part 3 of 3

﴿وَإِن جَـٰهَدَاكَ عَلَىٰٓ أَن تُشْرِكَ بِى مَا لَيْسَ لَكَ بِهِۦ عِلْمٌ فَلَا تُطِعْهُمَا ۖ وَصَاحِبْهُمَا فِى ٱلدُّنْيَا مَعْرُوفًا ۖ وَٱتَّبِعْ سَبِيلَ مَنْ أَنَابَ إِلَىَّ ۚ ثُمَّ إِلَىَّ مَرْجِعُكُمْ فَأُنَبِّئُكُم بِمَا كُنتُمْ تَعْمَلُونَ﴾

Translation of the meaning

But if they endeavor to make you associate with Me that of which you have no knowledge,[1161] do not obey them but accompany them in [this] world with appropriate kindness and follow the way of those who turn back to Me [in repentance]. Then to Me will be your return, and I will inform you about what you used to do.

Translator's notes

[1161] See footnote to 29:8.

Quran · Luqman 31:15

My son, help your father in his old age, and don’t grieve him as long as he lives. If he fails in understanding, have patience with him. Don’t dishonor him in your full strength.

Sirach · 3:12-13

World English Bible

﴿قَالَ لَا تَثْرِيبَ عَلَيْكُمُ ٱلْيَوْمَ ۖ يَغْفِرُ ٱللَّهُ لَكُمْ ۖ وَهُوَ أَرْحَمُ ٱلرَّٰحِمِينَ﴾

Translation of the meaning

He said, "No blame will there be upon you today. May Allāh forgive you; and He is the most merciful of the merciful.

Quran · Yusuf 12:92

Everything has two handles, one by which it may be borne, the other by which it may not. If your brother sin against you lay not hold of it by the handle of injustice, for by that it may not be borne: but rather by this, that he is your brother, the comrade of your youth; and thus you will lay hold on it so that it may be borne.

Stoic writings · Golden Sayings 174

Epictetus, Golden Sayings (Crossley)

Does justice end love? The verses do not say so. The verse takes the gravest case, parents pressing you to set a partner beside God: do not obey them in that, and keep them company in this world with kindness. Refusing one thing is not cutting a bond. The second verse gives the model: Joseph before the brothers who harmed him, no blame on you today. He states the truth and forgives. Justice and mercy can live in one house.

A question for you

What do the two verses ask of you together?

If you sayTruth with kindness.
ThenThat is what 31:15 joins in one sentence.
If you sayForgiveness.
ThenForgiveness from strength, as Joseph did. It stays your choice, and no one here imposes it.
If you sayAnd what about staying silent?
ThenThat has a question of its own.

The same in the other books
